butir.teks: On the Nobility of the Intellect

Know that this is among the things that need no laborious effort to make manifest, especially since the nobility of knowledge has already become evident earlier, and the intellect is the wellspring of knowledge, its place of rising, and its foundation. Knowledge stands in relation to it as the fruit to the tree, the light to the sun, and sight to the eye. So how could what is the means to happiness in this world and the Hereafter not be noble? Or how could it be doubted, when even the beast, despite the poverty of its discernment, is awed by the intellect, so much so that the largest of beasts in body, the fiercest in savagery, and the mightiest in assault, when it sees the form of a human being, is awed by him and fears him, because it senses that he holds sway over it through what he has been singled out with of the grasp of stratagems.

For this reason he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "The elder among his people is like the prophet among his community." (١) That is not because of the abundance of his wealth, nor the largeness of his body, nor any increase in his strength, but because of the increase in his experience, which is the fruit of his intellect.
For this reason you see the Turks, the Kurds, the uncouth Arabs, and the rest of creation, even though their rank is close to that of the beasts, revere elders by nature.

For this reason, when many of the obstinate set out to kill the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), then when their eyes fell upon him and they adorned their eyes, as with kohl, with his noble countenance, they were awed by him, and there appeared to them what shone on the surface of his face of the light of prophethood, even though that was hidden within his self as the intellect is hidden. So the nobility of the intellect is among what is perceived by necessity. The aim is only that we cite what the reports and verses have brought in mentioning its nobility. Allah has named it light in His saying, Most High. And He named the knowledge derived from it spirit, revelation, and life, so He says, Most High, ⟦QS 42:52⟧ And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says, ⟦QS 6:122⟧ Wherever He mentions light and darkness, He means by it knowledge and ignorance, as in His saying, ⟦QS 2:257⟧ And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "O people, understand from your Lord, and counsel one another to use the intellect, so that you may know what you have been commanded and what you have been forbidden. Know that it will aid you with your Lord, and know that the intelligent person is the one who obeyed Allah, even if he is ugly in appearance, of low standing, base in rank, and shabby in looks, and that the ignorant person is the one who disobeyed Allah Most High, even if he is handsome in appearance, of great standing, noble in rank, and fine in looks, eloquent and articulate. Monkeys and pigs are more intelligent in the sight of Allah Most High than the one who disobeys Him, so do not be deceived by the exaltation the people of this world give them, for they are among the losers." (٢)

And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "The first thing Allah created was the intellect. He said to it, 'Come forward,' and it came forward. Then He said to it, 'Turn back,' and it turned back. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, 'By My might and My majesty, I have not created a creature more honoured to Me than you. Through you I take, through you I give, through you I reward, and through you I punish.'" (٣)

If you say: if this intellect is an accident, how was it created before bodies? And if it is a substance, how can there be a substance that subsists by itself and does not occupy space? Then know that this belongs to the knowledge of unveiling ('ilm al-mukashafa), so it is not fitting to mention it with the knowledge of conduct ('ilm al-mu'amala), and our aim now is to mention the branches of knowledge of conduct.

From Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Some people praised a man in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) until they went to extremes. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "How is the man's intellect?" They said, "We tell you of his striving in worship and in kinds of good, and you ask us about his intellect?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The fool, through his ignorance, brings about more than the wickedness of
the wicked one. And the servants will be raised tomorrow in the degrees of nearness to their Lord only in proportion to their intellects. (١)

From 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "A man has not acquired anything like a surplus of intellect that guides its owner to guidance and turns him back from ruin. A servant's faith is not complete, nor is his religion upright, until his intellect is perfect." (٢) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "A man reaches through his good character the rank of the one who fasts and stands in prayer, and a man's good character is not complete until his intellect is complete. At that point his faith is complete, and he obeys his Lord and disobeys his enemy Iblis." (٣) From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Everything has a pillar, and the pillar of the believer is his intellect, so his worship is according to the measure of his intellect. Have you not heard the words of the wicked in the Fire, ⟦QS 67:10⟧" (٤) From 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said to Tamim ad-Dari, "What is chieftainship among you?" He answered, "The intellect." He said, "You have spoken truly. I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) as I have asked you, and he said what you have said. Then he said, 'I asked Jibril (peace be upon him), "What is chieftainship?" and he said, "The intellect."'" (٥) From al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: One day questions put to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) became many, and he said, "O people, everything has a mount, and a person's mount is the intellect. The best of you in guidance and in knowledge of the proof is the most excellent of you in intellect." (٦) From Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) returned from the battle of Uhud, he heard the people saying, "So-and-so is braver than so-and-so, and so-and-so fought a trial that so-and-so did not," and the like. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "As for this, you have no knowledge of it." They said, "How is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said (peace and blessings be upon him), "They fought according to the measure of the intellect Allah apportioned to them, and their help and their intention were according to their intellects. So those of them who were struck down were struck down in various ranks. When it is the Day of Resurrection, they will divide the ranks according to their intentions and their intellects." (٧) From al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The angels strove and exerted themselves in obedience to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, through the intellect, and the believers among the children of Adam strove according to their intellects. The most active of them in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the most abundant of them in intellect." (٨) From 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, by what do people excel one another in this world?" He said, "By the intellect." I said, "And in the Hereafter?" He said, "By the intellect." I said, "Are they not recompensed only for their deeds?" He said (peace and blessings be upon him), "O 'A'isha, did they do anything except according to what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave them of intellect? According to what they were given of intellect were their deeds, and according to what they did they are recompensed." (٩) From Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Everything has an instrument and equipment, and the instrument of the believer is the intellect. Everything has a mount, and a person's mount is the intellect. Everything has a pillar, and the pillar of the religion is the intellect. Every people has an aim, and the aim of the servants is the intellect. Every people has a caller, and the caller of the worshippers is the intellect. Every merchant has merchandise, and the merchandise of those who strive is the intellect. Every household has a steward, and the steward of the houses of the truthful ones is the intellect. And for every ruin

a rebuilding, and the rebuilding of the Hereafter is the intellect. Every person has descendants to whom he is ascribed and by whom he is remembered, and the descendants of the truthful ones, those who are ascribed to him and remembered by him, are the intellect. Every journey has a tent, and the tent of the believers is the intellect." (١) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "The most beloved of the believers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the one who toiled in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, was sincere towards His servants, perfected his intellect, and was sincere towards himself, so he saw clearly and acted upon it during the days of his life, and so succeeded and prospered." (٢) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "The most complete of you in intellect is the most intense of you in fear of Allah Most High, and the best of you in looking into what He has commanded you and forbidden, even if he is the least of you in voluntary worship." (٣)
